title: Japan's Vending Machines to Sell Canned Hot Pot
paragraphs: Japan is famous for its many vending machines. They sell drinks, snacks and many other things. Now, some of them will sell a new kind of hot food: hot pot soup in a can.
Hot pot, called "nabe" in Japanese, is a popular dish in Japan, especially in cold weather. People cook meat, fish and vegetables together in a big pot of soup at the table.

The new canned soup was made by two companies working together. Dydo is a drinks company that has many vending machines. Mizkan is a food company. It makes a popular soup base for hot pot called "Shimenabe."

There are two flavors. The first one is sesame and soy milk, made with chicken and vegetable soup. The second one is scallop and clam, made with a fish soup called "dashi." Both soups also have rice in them. This style of soup with rice is called "zosui" in Japanese. In Japan, many people like to add rice to the soup at the end of a hot pot meal.
Each can costs 160 yen, which is about one US dollar. The cans went on sale in vending machines and stores from October 26.
You do not need a bowl or a spoon to eat this soup. Like other vending machine drinks, people can drink it straight from the can.
The companies say the soups have a rich taste and a nice smell. They are a good snack for people who feel a little cold and a little hungry.
